paper_id: Language-Specific Layer Matters_ Efficient Multilingual Enhancement for Large Vision-Language Models
title: Language-Specific Layer Matters: Efficient Multilingual Enhancement for Large Vision-Language Models
motivation: LVLMs exhibit severe multilingual imbalance due to English-centric training corpora, limiting real-world global deployment.
problem_framing: Identify which model layers handle language-specific representations to enable targeted, efficient multilingual enhancement.
key_insight: Language-specific neuron activations concentrate in shallow decoder layers; fine-tuning only these layers achieves efficient multilingual alignment.
method_signature: PLAST: monitor neuron activation MSD to identify language-specific layers, then fine-tune only top-5 decoder layers with question-translation pairs.
evaluation_criteria: Average accuracy across 6 languages on MMBench/MMMB; parameter efficiency (tuned params ratio); training cost reduction vs full fine-tuning.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Performance trade-offs exist across languages due to pre-training data imbalances; larger-scale model experiments not conducted due to compute limits.
evidence_for_taste: shallow layers more engaged in learning language-specific representations
multilingual understanding is predominantly localized in the shallow layers
Precisely selecting layers that are actively involved in multilingual comprehension is essential
Indiscriminately fine-tuning all language-specific layers might compromise inherent general capabilities
thinking_moves: 从LLM的多语言机制研究迁移到LVLM，验证三层工作模式（语言理解→任务解决→语言转换）是否适用
用logit lens可视化和神经元激活统计（MSD）代替主观的layer selection假设
区分语言特定层vs任务解决层：前者用MSD衡量语言间激活差异，后者保持通用能力不被破坏
从full-parameter fine-tuning退回到layer-selective tuning，牺牲部分自由度换取效率提升
cites_own_work: Fan et al., 2025 (语言特异性神经元研究)
